title: Transplant Readiness and Hardening-Off
objective: Decide when a seedling can move systems and acclimate it to changed light, wind, temperature, humidity, and root-zone conditions.

terms.definition: State in which roots, shoot, water balance, and health support movement into the next production environment.
Gradual acclimation to a more demanding environment before final transplant.
Degree to which roots and medium remain coherent during removal and placement.
Temporary or lasting growth reduction after root disturbance and environmental change.

coreScience: Readiness is not an exact plant age. A transplantable seedling has active new growth, an intact apex, a root system that holds or occupies the propagation unit without being severely bound, manageable water demand, and no unresolved disease or pest issue. The receiving environment must also be prepared.

Transplant changes multiple variables at once: container volume, media chemistry, moisture distribution, root-zone oxygen, light, temperature, humidity, airflow, and sometimes outdoor ultraviolet and wind. Hardening-off reduces the size of that step by gradually increasing exposure while monitoring water balance and injury.

Root disturbance can damage fine absorptive tissue and temporarily alter establishment, but severity depends on plug integrity, method, and recovery conditions. Use an internal transplant procedure: preserve the root ball, match plug and receiving-media contact, avoid unsupported burial of injured stem tissue, and document planting depth, compaction, irrigation, and solution EC. These are project controls, not universal cannabis thresholds.
cultivationRelevance: Prepare and verify the destination before removing seedlings from trays. Match media moisture on both sides of the interface, preserve labels, and record the new container or bed position.
For outdoor movement, use staged exposure to brighter light, wind, temperature swings, and lower humidity. Pause or step back if leaves scorch, wilt persistently, stems lodge, or growth stops.

measureAndRecord.requirement: True-leaf growth, root occupation, plug integrity, health, and irrigation status.
Container or bed ID, media batch, prewet condition, environment, and spacing.
Daily duration, light or outdoor exposure, temperature, wind, and response.
Date, operator, depth, root disturbance, label verification, and initial irrigation.
Turgor, new growth, root-zone moisture, injury, survival, and days to resumed growth.

misconceptions: A fixed number of days determines readiness: Development and root occupation vary with genotype and environment.
Hardening means deliberately severe wilting: Acclimation should challenge gradually without preventable injury.
Bigger containers eliminate transplant stress: Media interface, water distribution, root handling, and environment still matter.
evidenceLimits: General hardening schedules are starting frameworks. Cannabis response, weather, greenhouse conditions, and receiving systems require local adjustment.
